text:
maria: Heads-up, eu-west1 just had a big spike to hosted API (proms showing 10x requests). Autoscaler tried 3 scale-ups to gpu-pool-eu-west1 but instances stayed in ProvisioningPending. We saw ~20s 503s and fallback to cpu-only route. Investigating. :rotating_light:

autoscale-bot: [ALERT] pool=eu-west1-gpu attempt=3 status=FAILED reason=InstanceProvisionerTimeout details=attach-driver-timeout

devin: Can you paste the provisioner logs and the cluster-provisioner status? Any quota errors?

maria: Pasting the last relevant chunk from cluster-provisioner logs:
```
2026-03-18T12:15:02Z ProvisionerController reconcile pool=eu-west1-gpu attempt=3
2026-03-18T12:15:17Z InstanceProvisioner: creating instance id=inst-79
2026-03-18T12:20:18Z InstanceProvisioner: attach-driver timeout after 300s
2026-03-18T12:20:18Z ERROR QuotaError: GPUs available=0 requested=4
2026-03-18T12:20:18Z InstanceProvisioner: marking instance inst-79 FAILED
```

samir: looks like two things: 1) regional GPU quota is exhausted in eu-west1 (quota shows 0), 2) nodes are failing the nvidia-driver install and hitting attach-driver timeout which blocks the provisioner. The quota explains the repeated failures.

kai: Confirming driver issue on new kernels: dmsg from node-init shows kernel-module build failed -> image mismatch with the driver bundle we ship. Quick snippet:
```
+ /usr/local/bin/nvidia-installer --silent
ERROR: Unable to find a kernel module matching kernel 6.2.11-rt
```

maria: Ok. Immediate mitigation: I paused autoscaler for pool eu-west1-gpu (patched scaling.policy.paused=true) to stop thrash and stop wasting API calls. I also opened a short-term reserved capacity request in eu-central1 (resv-12345) and started shifting traffic gradually.

autoscale-bot: Scale paused by maria at 1834567905 (reason: provisioning failures, stop thrash).

devin: When you shift traffic keep an eye on edge rate limits — last time shifting region-wide we hit per-region route caps and got 429s. How much headroom does eu-central1 have on the edge layer?

samir: eu-central1 has ~600 rps free on the primary route before hitting 429 per-edge-config. If we shard traffic by customer with sticky routing we can avoid global thundering. Suggest rolling 10% increments every 30s.

kai: For the driver problem: I'm building a patched driver bundle compatible with the new kernel and will push to staging node image repo. ETA 45m. Until then we should avoid spinning new GPU nodes in eu-west1.

maria: Plan implemented: 1) paused autoscaler for affected pool, 2) activated reserved capacity in eu-central1, 3) started 10% traffic shift to eu-central1 (manual routing override), 4) disabled automatic fallback to large-models to avoid extra GPU pressure. Monitoring dashboards: token latency, 5xx rate, provisioner queue length.

devin: Noting cost impact: reserved capacity + cross-region egress will spike cost today. Logging cost estimate in incident ticket.

samir: Temporary routing tweak (applied):
```yaml
routing:
  region_shift:
    eu-west1: weight: 0.6
    eu-central1: weight: 0.4
  sticky_by: customer_id
  gradual_step: 0.1
```

maria: Can infra-oncall open an incident and assign postmortem owner? Also we need follow-ups: quota request for eu-west1, validate node-init image compatibility, add metric that counts "provisioner attach-driver timeouts" as SLO signal.

infra-oncall: Incident INC-2026-034 opened, assigned to @kai for driver fix and @samir for routing/capacity follow-up. Postmortem owner: @maria.

maria: Action items (short):
- kai: deliver patched GPU driver bundle (ETA 45m)
- samir: request quota bump and coordinate reserved capacity (ETA 2h)
- devin: cost tracking and notify finance on expected spike (ETA today EOD)
- infra: enable attach-driver-timeout alert to pager (low latency)

maria: I'll keep this thread updated as we make progress. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
